## Part A -- anatomy of the superseded 2 ms brownout branch

One variable: the DUT netlist. PVT point `tt_27c_3.63v` --
one of the three corners where record `20260811-063744-5ff219c` reads
`ok_bo_end_droop_mv` = 3630 mV. Rail shape is that record's own serialized
brownout branch (0.5 V dip, then a full collapse), held past the end of the
recovery instead of stopping at 2 ms.

| | schematic export | klt-extracted |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| BIAS_OK back above 1.4 V (capacitive, on the rail's return ramp) | -6.1 us after rail return | -6.1 us after rail return |
| …de-asserts BELOW 1.4 V at | 63.5 us after rail return | 771.8 us after rail return |
| …genuinely re-asserts at | 104.7 us after rail return | 884.4 us after rail return |
| VREF last more than 1 % from settled | 78.4 us after rail return | 790.9 us after rail return |
| BIAS_OK 1.4 V rising crossings after the collapse | 2 | 2 |
| V(BIAS_OK) at the record's 1.95 ms sample | 3.6299 V | 1.7136e-07 V |
| V(VREF) at the record's 1.95 ms sample | 1.199 V | 1.1991 V |
| V(VREF) settled | 1.199 V | 1.1991 V |

Times are relative to the rail reaching full value at 1.110 ms; the return ramp starts 10 µs earlier, which is why the first entry is negative.

### What Part A shows

1. **`BIAS_OK` is back above 1.4 V before the rail has even finished returning, on both netlists -- and that is a FALSE valid, not a recovery.** The high-impedance output is dragged up capacitively by the rail's own 10 µs return ramp while the reference is still parked, and it stays there for 777.9 us on the extracted netlist against 69.7 us on the schematic export -- a factor of 11.2. V(VREF) does not reach its settled value until 790.9 us after the return (extracted) versus 78.4 us (schematic). This is exactly the starved-loop window `design/bias_core.md` documents, and it is what `t_false_ok_brownout_us` measures.
2. **The 1.95 ms sample instant lands inside the notch where `BIAS_OK` is CORRECTLY low.** Confirmed: the extracted cell de-asserts at 771.8 us after the return and re-asserts at 884.4 us, and 1.95 ms sits between them, which is why `ok_bo_end_droop_mv` read 3630 mV there. The flag is doing its job at that instant: the settle detector has noticed the reference is wrong and pulled the flag down while the loop re-establishes itself.
3. **The schematic export is not qualitatively different, only faster.** It has the same three-phase shape -- capacitive false return, de-assert at 63.5 us, genuine re-assert at 104.7 us -- and the same notch; the notch has simply come and gone long before 1.95 ms, which is why the same check reads 0.075 mV there. Nothing about the mechanism is new post-layout; its TIME CONSTANT is.

## Part B -- latch test at the corners the 30 ms deck does not clear

One variable: none. These are the extracted netlist at the corners whose
`bo_*_ppm` still fail on the replacement deck, re-run on a 120 ms transient -- four times longer -- to separate *still
recovering* from *latched onto a second solution*.

Both times below are absolute, so they are directly comparable with the replacement deck's own 29.9 ms sample instant.

| corner | VREF recovered at | BIAS_OK re-asserts at | VREF at 119.9 ms | error vs. settled | false-valid time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `sf_-40c_3.30v` | 25.86 ms | 26.02 ms | 1.197847 V | +0.000 ppm | 24.22 ms |
| `sf_-40c_3.63v` | 30.95 ms | 31.10 ms | 1.197714 V | +0.000 ppm | 28.78 ms |

### What Part B shows

**Not latched.** Every corner recovers, and the reference returns to within 0.000 ppm of the value it held before the event -- inside the ±500 ppm bound `bo_deep_ppm` applies, at a point where that check FAILS on the 30 ms deck. What that failure reports is the recovery still being in progress at the sample instant (slowest recovery here: 30.95 ms absolute), not a second stable solution. The reproducibility claim `bo_*_ppm` exists to make therefore holds; the check reads FAIL because the *timing* it shares a sample point with does not, and that is the honest answer rather than a reason to lengthen the deck until it goes green.

**This control deck reproduces the graded one, so the remaining failure is real rather than an artefact of the longer run.** At `sf_-40c_3.30v` the 30 ms record measures `t_bo_recover_us` = 24916.7 us, i.e. an absolute re-assert at 26.03 ms; this 120 ms control puts the same edge at 26.02 ms -- agreement to 10 us on a 26 ms measurement, despite this deck running a 20 us print step against the graded deck's 4 us. Recovery relative to the 29.9 ms sample (positive = recovered before it): `sf_-40c_3.30v` +4.04 ms; `sf_-40c_3.63v` -1.05 ms. The one failing corner misses by a clear ~1 ms, not by rounding.
